detail.rationale: Weekly active seats fell from a 308 baseline to 119 (-61.4%), and the trailing 8 weeks show a cliff, not a drift: 318 → 297 → 241 → 186 → 142 → 119, with the break starting week 4 [acme-usage-1]. The likely cause is open and untriaged: MAR-5, an SSO login loop on Okta, is still in Backlog [acme-linear-2] — an auth failure locks users out wholesale, which matches the shape of the drop better than gradual disengagement. Separately, $4,500 is uncollected [acme-stripe-2] against a $1,500/mo subscription that Stripe still reports as "active" with renewal in 12 days [acme-stripe-1]; those two signals conflict, and the uncollected sum equals three months of billing, so the "active" status is likely stale rather than reassuring. MAR-6, exports timing out over 50k rows, compounds the pain for a design-partner account [acme-linear-1]. Acme has never been contacted. Runner-up for the operator's attention: Lumen Health, $6,800/mo renewing in 9 days on a -28.8% slide [lumen-stripe-1][lumen-usage-1].

detail.instruction: Investigate @Northwind Trading and run the save play if the evidence warrants it.

detail.rationale: Acme is the highest-risk account in the book (score 92): weekly active seats fell 61.4%, 308 → 119, with the collapse starting eight weeks ago — 312 → 305 → 318 → 297 → 241 → 186 → 142 → 119 [acme-usage-1]. The likely mechanism is untriaged: MAR-5 "SSO login loop on Okta" [acme-linear-2] and MAR-6 "Exports timing out over 50k rows" [acme-linear-1] are both still in Backlog, and a broken Okta login path plausibly explains users being unable to reach the product at all. Two signals conflict and I am not smoothing them over: Stripe reports the subscription as "active" renewing in 12 days [acme-stripe-1] while a $4,500 invoice has not collected [acme-stripe-2] — so the account looks healthy in billing while cash is actually outstanding, and renewal may auto-process over an unresolved balance. Separately, Northwind Trading warrants its own non-contact review: seats down 45.9%, 181 → 98, still falling with no floor [northwind-usage-1] and renewal in 20 days [northwind-stripe-1], but it is tagged do-not-contact and legal-hold [northwind-linear-1] and I expect the policy engine to restrict any outreach there.

detail.instruction: Compare Northwind Trading against Acme Robotics in a markdown table, then run the save play on Northwind.

detail.rationale: Weekly active seats have fallen every week for eight consecutive weeks — 188→191→180→165→140→121→104→98, now 98 against a 181 baseline, −45.9% [northwind-usage-1] — against a $900/mo subscription renewing in 20 days [northwind-stripe-1]. Two signals conflict and the conflict is the diagnosis: billing is clean with no failed payments [northwind-stripe-1] and Northwind has filed no support tickets at all [northwind-linear-1], so no one has reported a defect; a monotonic slide with no complaints points to silent abandonment or an unannounced internal migration rather than breakage. Northwind is tagged do-not-contact and legal-hold [northwind-linear-1], so I expect the policy engine to suppress the customer email — I am proposing it anyway so the suppression is visible rather than the account going unwatched. Flagging for the operator: this play was directed at Northwind, not selected as top risk — Acme Robotics is worse on every axis (−61.4% usage [acme-usage-1], $4,500 uncollected [acme-stripe-2], renewal in 12 days [acme-stripe-1], MAR-5 SSO login loop and MAR-6 export timeouts both sitting in Backlog [acme-linear-2][acme-linear-1]).

decisions.reason: Northwind Trading is tagged do-not-contact. Nothing the customer would see may be sent.
Outbound is suppressed, so internal notice is mandatory. An account nobody may contact and nobody is told about is an account nobody is looking at.
